text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated 5xx/errors from services in us-west-2 (az9) for IPv6 egress. Auto-escalation to on-call (S1).

sara: saw the page, looking. oncall now. can someone paste the earliest traces? any customer reports?

matt: putting packet captures here — took tcpdump on a failing pod egress: 
```
14:12:03.123456 IP6 fe80::1 > 2606:4700:3030::ac: ICMP6, type 2 (Packet Too Big), mtu 1280
14:12:03.123457 IP6 fe80::1 > 2606:4700:3030::ac: ICMP6, type 2 (Packet Too Big), mtu 1280
```
we're seeing ICMPv6 "Packet Too Big" messages but client stacks aren't reducing MSS, connections hang and gRPC retries balloon.

ajay: sounds like PMTUD failure where routers respond but something strips or suppresses the ICMPv6 on the path back. I've seen this when edge firewalls rate-limit ICMPv6 or when jumbo frames are mismatched between AZ transit switches.

sara: scope? only az9 or multi-az? quick check on our latency dash: only az9 (hosted nodes in us-west-2-az9) show spike for ipv6-only endpoints. ipv4 flows look normal.

support-lead: seeing ~12 customer incidents opened over the last 15m, mostly gRPC timeouts to our embeddings service. A couple customers reported file uploads hang (multipart over ipv6). Impacted: cust-112, cust-227, cust-998. Marking P1-ish.

matt: additional evidence: curl -6 -v to one of our frontends times out after TLS handshake starts. packet trace shows server sent ICMPv6 PTB but client never adjusts (MSS still > path MTU). snippet: 
```
$ curl -6 -v https://api.redwood.dev/health
* Connected to api.redwood.dev (2606:...) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.3 handshake...
* Received unexpected EOF
```

cloud-network-eng: I pulled flow logs — a subset of transit routers in az9 are emitting ICMPv6 PTB with mtu 1280, but edge balancers are dropping fragmented fragments or blocking subsequent probe packets. We've reached out to cloud provider NOC (ticket CW-49821).

ajay: immediate mitigation I suggest: enable MSS clamping on affected host interfaces and LB egress to 1220 to give slack, and temporarily prefer IPv4 for control-plane RPCs. Commands to add on hosts (run via runbook): 
```
# on Linux hosts
ip -6 route change default dev eth0 mtu 1220
# or ip6tables to clamp
ip6tables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN SYN -j TCPMSS --set-mss 1220
```

sara: applying ip6tables clamp on two edge nodes now, rolling via canary: edge-az9-1 then -2. will monitor.

ops-rotation-bot: handoff note: sara (S1) -> erica (S1 backup) at 14:30 UTC. Erica please ack when you take over.

erica: acked, taking over at 14:30. thanks for the handoff. any live customer comms updated?

support-lead: posted status update to status.redwood.dev that we have IPv6 connectivity issues impacting a subset of customers in us-west-2; suggested workaround: use IPv4 endpoints for now. I'll update with customer list and our mitigation steps.

matt: clamp rolled to canary edge-az9-1: instant drop in errors on that node. metrics: 5xx -> baseline in ~2 min. rolling to second node.

sara: second canary looks good. rolling to remaining edges in az9. leaving preference routing unchanged for now but will throttle v6 on control-plane if needed.

cloud-network-eng: cloud provider responded: they observed a linecard CPU protection feature that is silently dropping ICMPv6 fragments under congestion (aimed at DDoS mitigation). They will disable the aggressive suppression for our tenant as an exception, but that will take ~45-60m for ops change. Their mitigation: ensure edge hosts clamp MSS for now and avoid large initial TCP windows.

erica: since provider ETA is ~1h, we'll keep host-level clamps as durable fix and add a BGP route change if needed. Action items for postmortem: 1) understand why clients didn't respond to PTB (client stack bug vs suppressed probes), 2) add automated MSS clamp when we detect PTB floods, 3) add runbook step to prefer v4 for control-plane during AZ network instability.

support-lead: emailed top-affected customers with current workaround and ETA. Recording incident as 'partial outage, ipv6 PMTUD suppression in us-west-2-az9' and setting a follow-up bridge at 15:30 for post-incident review.

matt: logs retention note — saving tcpdumps and flow logs to sec/incidents/1799998888/ for postmortem. command used: 
```
tcpdump -i any ip6 and icmp6 -w /tmp/az9-pmtud-1799998888.pcap
```

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-az9-ipv6-pmtud ; priority P1 ; responders: sara, erica, ajay, matt ; bridge: https://meet.redwood.dev/INC-2026

erica: summary for handoff to SRE on-call for overnight: provider change may take until 15:00 UTC, leave host clamps in place, monitor ipv6 5xx, if recurrence after provider change revert clamps and run deeper packet-level debug. I'll draft the postmortem template.

sara: thanks team — keeping channel open until provider confirms and all hosts stable. :white_check_mark:
